articles.title: Industry Takedown of Botnet Hidden in More Than 1.3 Million TV Set-Top Boxes across 200 Countries
articles.context: It's proof that collaboration is one of the most powerful tools we have against threats that cross borders and industries
articles.full_text:
Google, Plume, TrendAI™, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Synthient and Japan's National Police Agency form coordinated effort combining security research, threat intelligence and network expertise to identify and disrupt X.CPE botnet

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, a group of private and public sector partners announced a coordinated takedown of X.CPE, a global botnet hidden in more than 1.3 million set-top boxes across more than 200 countries. Hidden on devices before they were ever sold, the botnet used subscribers' devices and home internet connections without their knowledge or consent. This takedown was led by Google, Plume, TrendAI™, Lumen, HUMAN Security and Synthient, along with Japan's National Police Agency.

"Operations like this raise the cost for criminals and show that the infrastructure they rely on isn't out of reach," said Charley Snyder, Head of Disruption Operations at Google Threat Intelligence Group. "Disrupting X.CPE took partners across industry working together. It's proof that collaboration is one of the most powerful tools we have against threats that cross borders and industries."

A familiar device hiding an unfamiliar threat

X.CPE was embedded in firmware, the software that controls a device's basic operations, before set-top boxes reached subscribers' homes. X.CPE was built to evade pre-release security checks, and Google has since updated its review process in response, as well as banned the responsible OEM and any future subsidiaries or affiliates from making devices with preloaded Google apps. Unlike infections that depend on a user opening a suspicious attachment or installing an application, this threat arrived as part of the device itself. Subscribers received no consent request, notification or opt-out options.

Google, Plume, TrendAI™, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Synthient, working with Japan's National Police Agency, carried out a coordinated disruption campaign against X.CPE. Each organization contributed in its own way, applying its expertise in connected-device security, malware analysis, network visibility and digital fraud to analyze the botnet and disrupt its operations.

Together they dismantled a threat hiding behind seemingly routine device activity: software embedded in TV set-top boxes that gave botnet controllers remote access and allowed them to exploit home broadband connections without subscriber consent. The takedown also disrupted the command-and-control domains that operate the criminal affiliates' malware modules. Because these affiliates distribute their modules through channels beyond X.CPE, Google assesses that taking down these domains will sever access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices.

The effort demonstrates the importance of connecting intelligence across organizations to confront threats that cross technology and network boundaries. By bringing together distinct perspectives on compromised devices, malicious software and internet traffic, the partners supported a coordinated takedown aimed at disrupting unauthorized access and monetization and addressing risks to subscriber privacy, broadband resources and trust in connected devices.

Turning home broadband into a business without permission

The botnet generated revenue from compromised devices in a variety of ways, including: reselling bandwidth, delivering video content, ad fraud, loading additional backdoors and, in earlier versions, installing apps for payment.

Residential proxy software allowed third-party traffic to pass through subscribers' internet connections, using their home internet addresses and bandwidth without permission. Researchers also found collection of device, network and account information, alongside persistent remote access capabilities.

For service providers, the findings highlight a supply chain risk that may not be apparent from a device's everyday performance. A functioning streaming box can still generate unexplained traffic and undermine trust in the broadband service.

"Protecting the connected home requires visibility into threats that subscribers cannot see and should not be expected to detect," said Chris Griffiths, Chief Technology Officer at Plume. "By contributing broadband intelligence to this joint effort, we helped expose hidden supply chain risks and support coordinated action to make networks safer for service providers and their subscribers."

Complementary expertise, coordinated action

The partners contributed to the Google-led effort to disrupt X.CPE:

TrendAI™ Robert McArdle, Director of Cybercrime Research at TrendAI™ "We applaud Google's decisive action in removing this threat. Our research identified over 1.3 million devices affected by this campaign. That's millions of households and businesses completely unaware that their equipment was being used as an accessory in active criminality - whether defrauding advertisers or piggybacking on their connections to carry out other attacks via residential proxies - which would commonly include identity theft impersonating people in their region. This action by Google and research partners significantly sets back these attackers, and TrendAI research will be watching them closely if they attempt to rebuild."

HUMAN Gavin Reid, CISO at HUMAN "Compromised-device networks are sustained by profit: operators take control of devices and household connections without consent, then monetise that access through proxy services and various fraud activities. Group action, as exemplified in this operation, interrupts the infrastructure needed for monetisation, raising the cost of operating these networks and weakening the incentives that sustain them. "

SYNTHIENT Benjamin Brundage, CEO at Synthient. "Illicit pay-per-install networks provide a significant backbone to the larger fraud ecosystem, powering everything from direct ad fraud to unregulated proxy networks that push credential stuffing and DDoS botnets. The takedown of X.Cpe helps protect this space as a whole, as well as the unsuspecting consumers victimized by this scheme." - Benjamin Brundage

Research and resources:

Google: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/shutting-the-door-on-the-xcpe-botnet Plume: http://www.plume.com/xcpe-botnet-whitepaper-pdf TrendAI™: https://www.trendaisecurity.com/en-us/resources-insights/trendai-security-blog/trendaitm-research-helps-disrupt-android-tv-botnet-of-more-than-13-million-pre-infected-devices

These customers have transformed how they approach risk, turning threat intelligence into innovation, and weaving security into the fabric of business strategy. That's what true excellence looks like."

At SoftBank, we are committed to advancing cybersecurity as a critical foundation for driving social and industrial transformation through cutting-edge technologies, including AI. articles.title: TrendAI™ Brings AI-Driven Security That Runs Entirely Under Customer Control to Sovereign and Private Clouds with NVIDIA Nemotron™ Open Models
articles.context: TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security...
articles.full_text:
TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security data ever leaving the sovereign boundary.

DALLAS, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced it is bringing NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC), building on its collaboration with NVIDIA. The integration brings AI-assisted security operations into customer-controlled environments, extending capabilities such as guided investigation, security reasoning, and agentic SIEM to organizations with sovereignty, data residency and operational control.

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today, enabling organizations to deploy TrendAI Vision One™ in customer-controlled private cloud, sovereign cloud and on-premises environments. The Nemotron integration extends AI-assisted security operations into these environments while maintaining customer control over security data and deployment.

Why Open Models Matter for SovereigntyHighly regulated organizations need AI-driven security that fits their data-control requirements. Nemotron open models can support these requirements by bringing the model to the data rather than the data to the model. Customers decide where the model runs, which version is deployed, and who can access it, running AI-powered security operations on NVIDIA accelerated computing in their own data centers, sovereign clouds, and restricted-connectivity environments. TrendAI™ collaboration with NVIDIA on OpenShell provides an additional level of security for agents, ensuring organizations have control and visibility of agentic activities.

Who Controls the Intelligence Acting on Your Data?"Sovereignty extends beyond where data resides. Enterprises also need control over where the intelligence acting on that data operates, and how it is governed." says Rachel Jin, CEO, TrendAI™. "Organizations shouldn't have to give up the operational benefits of AI because their security data and operations need to remain within a customer-controlled environment. Our work is about bringing AI-powered security operations to the environments our customers choose to control."

"Open models give organizations the transparency and control to run on their own terms, which is critical for sovereign environments," said John Fanelli, Vice President, Enterprise Software at NVIDIA. "TrendAI's integration of NVIDIA Nemotron models enables enterprises to put their most sensitive data to work, without it ever leaving their control."

Customer Perspective: Sovereignty Without CompromiseTITECH, which delivers sovereign security operations to customers in Oman, is working with TrendAI™ as a design partner on the Nemotron integration ahead of general availability.

"TrendAI Vision One for Sovereign and Private Cloud has provided our local customers in Oman with a trusted foundation for keeping security operations under customer control while complying with country data residency regulations," says TITECH CEO, Mohammed Hassan. "Nemotron-powered capabilities will let us offer advanced threat analysis and AI-assisted security operations to our customers while maintaining data sovereignty and operational control."

The integration supports AI-assisted threat analysis, policy-based response, and guided security operations within customer-controlled environments. These capabilities help organizations improve security operations with AI while maintaining control over where security data and AI processing reside.

Customer Outcome: Security and control from the start"As enterprises apply AI to real-world deployment, security and control must be embedded into the infrastructure from day one," says Business Manager of Security at Bechtle AG, Mathias Schick. "Our customers want to harness the full potential of AI without compromising data sovereignty, security, or operational control. Integrating AI-powered security into sovereign and private-cloud environments is an important step toward enabling secure AI adoption at scale, particularly for organizations with stringent security and compliance requirements."

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) with NVIDIA Nemotron integration supports:

Customer-controlled AI: NVIDIA Nemotron open models deployed and run on customer-controlled infrastructure, with no dependency on external inference services

AI-assisted threat analysis: Reasoning across security signals to identify complex threat patterns, attack chains, and AI-native attack paths

Policy-based threat response: Supporting protective actions through organization-defined policies and security-team controls

Guided security operations: Helping security teams investigate threats and prioritize response activities

Agentic SIEM capabilities: Correlating telemetry and assisting with security reasoning while maintaining team oversight

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today. Visit trendaisecurity.com/platform/sovereign-private-cloud or visit TrendAI™ at NVIDIA GTC Berlin's expo (October 21-22, 2026) to preview these planned capabilities.

articles.title: Trend Micro Announces Up to ¥10 Billion toward Cyber Resilience Initiative to Strengthen Security for Japanese Organizations in the AI Era
articles.context: The growing threat extends beyond large enterprises and critical infrastructure to smaller businesses, suppliers and service providers that form the foundation of Japan's economy
articles.full_text:
Initiative supports nationwide modernization of security measures for individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises, with additional access to TrendAI Vision One™ AI security capabilities and expert technical support provided through partners.

TOKYO, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trend Micro Incorporated (TSE: 4704) today announced plans for the Japan Cyber Resilience Initiative, a major national effort to help Japanese organizations strengthen their cybersecurity, reduce critical exposures and modernize their defenses for the AI era. This initiative is designed to support not only organizations but also individuals.

Japan's cybersecurity challenge is escalating rapidly. According to threat research from TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, 607 publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents were recorded during the first nine months of 2026, already exceeding the 594 reported throughout all of 2025*. Furthermore, the growing number of personal data breaches at organizations has exposed sensitive information on a large scale, creating cyber risks not only for enterprises but also for individuals and Japanese society as a whole.

*Cybersecurity incident figures are tallies as of October 9, 2026. Figures may change due to factors such as incidents that are later disclosed retroactively and additional cases being added.

Yet as attacks grow in volume and sophistication, many organizations remain unprepared for the next generation of threats. The growing threat extends beyond large enterprises and critical infrastructure to smaller businesses, suppliers and service providers that form the foundation of Japan's economy.

The program is designed to serve organizations and individuals across Japan, with an initial emphasis on critical infrastructure, major enterprises and the smaller businesses essential to their supply chains. Support will be provided in phases, tailored to organizational needs, eligibility and available resources.

Trend Micro will work closely with its extensive network of channel partners, systems integrators and managed service providers across Japan to extend the initiative's reach. Eligible organizations will receive up to 10 days of professional services free of charge*, delivered through partners to help them access the right cybersecurity expertise and support.

*For details, including requirements for use, please contact us.

Through its enterprise cybersecurity business, TrendAI™, the company proposes to make available up to ¥10 billion in TrendAI Flex licensing credits to help eligible organizations modernize their security environments with TrendAI Vision One™. The initiative also includes plans to mobilize forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) and provide access to managed detection and response (MDR) expertise.

A national challenge demands a national commitment

Japan's senior political leaders have characterized the situation as a cybersecurity emergency.

As a global cybersecurity company headquartered in Japan, Trend Micro has spent decades protecting Japanese businesses while investing extensively in global threat research, vulnerability discovery, threat intelligence and incident response.

"Japan is our home. When the organizations and individuals that power our economy, our infrastructure and our communities face an escalating cybersecurity challenge, we have a responsibility to step forward. No organization should have to face this challenge alone. We are bringing together our technology, our people and our global security expertise to help Japan strengthen its defenses today and prepare for a future in which cyber threats will move faster than ever." said Eva Chen, Trend Micro CEO.

The Japan Cyber Resilience Initiative will provide the following six forms of support to organizations and individuals.

＜For organizations＞

1. Up to ¥10 billion to accelerate cybersecurity modernization

Trend Micro proposes an aggregate allocation of up to ¥10 billion in TrendAI Flex licensing credits to help eligible organizations adopt and expand protection through the TrendAI Vision One™ platform designed to help customers modernize their existing security environments, strengthen protection across critical systems. Through TrendAI Flex Unlimited, customers will also be able to access additional TrendAI Vision One™ capabilities, including AI security innovations.

The initiative will also help existing customers, working with their trusted channel partners where appropriate, build on their current security investments and transition toward modern, AI-era defenses without unnecessarily disrupting established protection.

The proposed allocation represents licensing credits, not a cash grant. The initiative will be introduced in phases, with detailed eligibility criteria, credit allocation and redemption terms, partner participation options, and service availability to be communicated as the program is rolled out.

2. Forward-deployed engineers to turn technology into stronger defenses

Recognizing that cybersecurity modernization requires more than technology alone, TrendAI™ plans to mobilize forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) and technical specialists to work directly with participating organizations.

These specialists will work alongside participating organizations and their existing partners, where appropriate, to assess critical exposures, identify security gaps, prioritize risk reduction and accelerate the deployment of modern security capabilities.

FDE engagements will initially prioritize organizations whose security is particularly important to national infrastructure, economic activity and interconnected supply chains. For smaller organizations, Trend Micro intends to work through appropriate delivery models and its partner ecosystem to help extend the initiative's reach.

3. Expert-led detection, response and operational resilience

Through TrendAI™'s MDR capabilities and security expertise, eligible organizations will be able to explore additional support for continuous threat monitoring, incident investigation and response.

The initiative aims to help organizations move beyond isolated security controls toward a coordinated approach that connects exposure management, threat detection, incident response and proactive risk reduction.

Trend Micro also protects more than 10 million consumers across Japan through its TrendLife™ business unit. Through local partners and a network of managed service provider (MSP) partners serving over 230,000 small and medium-sized businesses, we also help protect close to 2 million business devices. Building on this foundation, we will continue to help strengthen security for consumers and small businesses alike.

4. 60-day free trial of Worry-Free Business Security Services provided (TBD)

Small and medium-sized businesses play a vital role in supply chains, and strengthening their security is increasingly urgent. For these customers, a 60-day free trial of Worry-Free Business Security Services will be provided. In addition, TrendLife™ is considering new support for the Worry-Free series together with its channel partners. Further details will be announced as they are finalized. Note: The free trial is available only to new customers in Japan and must be started by December 31, 2026.

5. Exploring AI-Powered Scam Protection to Strengthen Digital Trust on LINE

As small businesses increasingly rely on LINE Official Accounts (LINE OA) to engage with customers, everyday interactions may also expose them to scams disguised as customer inquiries, suspicious links, or fraudulent requests.

TrendLife™ is advancing API integrations with providers of LINE-related services, enabling AI-powered scam detection capabilities to be seamlessly embedded into customer touchpoints and helping strengthen protection for both businesses and their customers. We are currently working with partners, including Crescendo Lab, one of Asia's leading LINE CRM providers, and are in the final stages of preparation for commercial deployment by the end of the year.

＜For consumers＞

6. 90 days of Trend Micro ScamCheck provided free of charge

TrendLife™ will provide 90 days of complimentary access to Trend Micro ScamCheck, our mobile scam protection app. In the event that leaked personal information is misused in phone, email, or other scam attempts, Trend Micro ScamCheck helps protect users from potential scams.

The benefit will be provided through the following channels:

TrendLife Online Store: Customers who purchase through the site below will have their subscription extended by 90 days. https://shop.trendlife.com/ja-jp/products/scam-buster.asp

App stores: Please follow the instructions on the page below. https://trendlife.com/ja-jp/blog/news-tmsc-3-month-free-trial/

Note: In all cases, customers must start using the service by December 31, 2026. This offer is available only to customers in Japan.

A lasting commitment to Japan's cyber resilience

Trend Micro will work with customers and partners to translate this initiative into measurable improvements in cybersecurity, with plans to track participation, modernization progress and defensive outcomes.

Organizations and partners interested in participating can contact their Trend Micro representative or visit the Initiative Landing Page to register their interest and receive updates as program details and participation opportunities become available. For individual customers, please contact us through TrendLife™ website.

About Trend Micro

Trend Micro Incorporated is a Japan-headquartered global cybersecurity company dedicated to protecting the digital world. Drawing on decades of security expertise, worldwide threat intelligence and cybersecurity innovation, the company helps organizations and individuals protect their digital environments and build resilience against evolving cyber threats.

For more information, visit trendmicro.com or TrendLife™ (Japanese).

articles.title: TrendAI™ Zero Day Initiative™ awards over $1.2 million at Pwn2Own
articles.context: Ethical hackers discovered 98 unique zero-day vulnerabilities at the three-day event, advancing the techniques defenders use to find and fix flaws at AI speed CORK, Ireland, Oct
articles.full_text:
Ethical hackers discovered 98 unique zero-day vulnerabilities at the three-day event, advancing the techniques defenders use to find and fix flaws at AI speed

CORK, Ireland, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader from Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today celebrated the efforts of the global security research community at Pwn2Own Ireland by awarding a total of $1,262,000 in prizes. Contestants discovered and disclosed 98 unique zero-day vulnerabilities across categories including: mobile phones; smart home devices; wellness; printers; messaging; AI infrastructure; and AI coding agents.

Dustin Childs, Head of Threat Awareness at TrendAI's Zero Day Initiative: "The vulnerabilities discovered at Pwn2Own are sent to vendors so they can patch them quickly. Having visibility into these vulnerabilities also helps protect TrendAI customers via virtual patching. The lasting value of an event like this is what defenders learn. Every exploit chain demonstrated on stage teaches us something new about how modern systems break, and those lessons go directly into how we train our own research capability to discover, validate and remediate the next one faster. As AI tools and infrastructure continue to become central to business functions, staying ahead of vulnerabilities will be as critical as ever."

The devices on stage at Pwn2Own are deliberately familiar—phones, printers, smart home hubs, wearables—and that familiarity is the point. Watching a researcher chain several flaws together to take over a consumer phone makes visible a process that usually happens out of sight. It is the same process, and often the same class of flaw, that applies to the enterprise-grade systems behind global ecommerce, banking, critical infrastructure and healthcare.

The disclosures made through TrendAI™ ZDI at Pwn2Own and year-round allow vendors to quickly understand and fix vulnerabilities before cybercriminals exploit them, ultimately benefiting organizations and end users of the impacted software or hardware. TrendAI™ research has shown that vendors are increasingly neglecting to patch software vulnerabilities that are disclosed to them. Through the TrendAI™ ZDI coordinated disclosure process, TrendAI Vision One™ customers are protected an average of 115 days ahead of the rest of the industry.

Caroline Kiel, CEO, PingUs: "Watching live zero-day exploits demonstrated on stage was exciting. It was encouraging to see the vendors be onsite to encourage the researcher community to poke holes in their products. Seeing how Pwn2Own turns fresh vulnerability research into immediate protection proves how deeply committed TrendAI is to securing products across the entire ecosystem."

Highlights from the event included:

Ikotas Labs, Inc. earned the title, Master of Pwn and $300,000, after it chained multiple issues together to successfully exploit the Google Pixel 10 at the very end of the three-day competition. Ikotas Labs, Inc. is the first-ever Japanese team to claim the Master of Pwn title.

Xint, which placed second in the competition, earned $150,000 by successfully demonstrating a remote exploit of the Google Pixel 10 through a single bug collision.

Interrupt Labs earned $5,000 after it successfully took over the Lexmark CX532adwe printer and played DOOM on its screen.

The next Pwn2Own competition is expected in early 2027. For more details, please visit: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/blog

articles.title: Ransomware Attacks Have Swept Japan. A.I. May Be Making Them Easier.
TrendAI™ Research Reinforces Japan's Urgent Cybersecurity Warning as Incidents Surge in 2026
articles.context: " TrendAI™ Forward-Looking Threat Research data shows Japan recorded more publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of 2026 than in all of 2025
articles.full_text:
Japan-headquartered cybersecurity leader shares threat intelligence and practical guidance as AI accelerates the global threat landscape.

DALLAS, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today issued a threat advisory for organizations in Japan after Masaaki Taira, who chairs the Liberal Democratic Party's National Cybersecurity Strategy Headquarters, said that "cyberspace is in a state of emergency." TrendAI™ Forward-Looking Threat Research data shows Japan recorded more publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of 2026 than in all of 2025. September alone saw 86 incidents, up about 18% from August and 37% from July.

The party's headquarters met on Oct. 9 in response to a series of cyberattacks on Japanese businesses and called on the government to strengthen public-private cooperation. Breaches at retailers, financial services firms, a car-sharing service and a rail operator have exposed data of millions of customers. The government's National Cybersecurity Office has sent guidance to ministries, local governments and private companies on keeping security protection up to date, using strong passwords and tightening security across supply chains.

The TrendAI™ Incident Response team has also seen a rise in incidents in Japan. In recent engagements, attackers exploited known vulnerabilities in public-facing applications to plant web shells on web servers, giving them a foothold from which they may attempt privilege escalation, lateral movement or access to connected databases. Japanese-language analysis of these cases from TrendAI™, along with hardening guidance, is available here.

"Cyberattacks are increasing globally, and so are the breaches and data leaks as a result. While AI might not be directly involved, its ability to help the attackers find targets and automate their operations makes cyberattacks scalable. Organizations need to shrink their cyber exposure and close the vulnerabilities in order to lower the odds of being victimized," said Ryan Flores, Co-lead, Forward-Looking Threat Research, TrendAI™.

AI is lowering the cost of attacks. TrendAI™ has not established a connection between the recent incidents in Japan and the use of AI by attackers. However, AI does let attackers accelerate reconnaissance, analyze vulnerabilities and produce convincing phishing in languages they do not speak. This weakens protections that languages, such as Japanese, once offered against foreign attackers. Automation also makes smaller organizations, including suppliers, more attractive targets given the increased return on investment for cybercriminals.

"While organizations around the world learn to work with their AI budgets, it's important to remember that AI has zero cost for cybercriminals," said Robert McArdle, Director, Forward-Looking Threat Research, TrendAI™. "There's already a robust economy for stolen accounts, APIs, and tokens, and this is driving the increasingly automated and agentic cybercrime campaigns we see today. The current surge in Japan should not be interpreted as a peak in criminal activity, it should be seen as the new baseline of attacks that will only increase in volume, speed, and relentlessness."

To harden protections, TrendAI™ recommends:

Patch internet-facing systems first. Keep an accurate inventory of public web servers, applications and cloud services, apply security updates promptly, prioritize vulnerabilities known to be actively exploited, and use virtual patching to cover the gap while fixes are tested and deployed.

Harden web servers. Restrict write access to application code, isolate file-upload directories, prevent uploaded content from running as scripts, and monitor for unauthorized changes to application files and configurations.

Watch database access. Monitor sensitive database operations and abnormal access patterns; run applications with minimum-privilege database accounts.

Check suppliers. Ask hosting and cloud providers how they would notify you of an incident, review which third parties hold customer data, and confirm critical services can recover independently of a single provider.

Strengthen identity verification. Review processes that rely solely on uploaded photographs of identity documents and adopt chip-based or other stronger verification consistent with regulatory guidance.

Bring AI usage into scope. Identify AI applications, models, and agents used across the organization, assess their provenance and reputation, review their access to sensitive data and internal systems, and apply appropriate security controls and approval processes.
